title: 0.74 and still PASS
spec: M18 · what a green suite does not tell you
intro: Twenty eval cases, twenty passes, overall 0.943. One of those passes got the entity half wrong. Find it, then look at why the regression gate had nothing to say about it.
foot: Run it for real: cd labs/M18-evaluation-testing/solution && python eval_runner.py

steps.title: Twenty cases, three scorers each
narrative: The dataset is 20 UCC research cases across four categories. Every case is scored three ways: task completion (did the answer contain the right filing numbers), entity resolution (did it name the right companies), and Claude-as-judge (a model grading accuracy, completeness and clarity).
overall is the plain mean of the three. Nothing is weighted, nothing is category-aware. Hold on to that — it is where the problem in step 3 comes from.
steps.youDo: Run python eval_runner.py and watch the twenty result lines stream past before the report renders.

steps.title: Case 17 — the one that passed anyway
narrative: Line 17 of the stream is EC-001: "Find all filings for XYZ Nonexistent Industries." The scorers disagree sharply. Task completion is 1.00 — the agent correctly returned no filings. Entity resolution is 0.50. The judge gives 0.73.
Mean of 1.00, 0.50 and 0.73 is 0.743, printed as 0.74. The pass threshold is 0.600. So the line reads PASS, the suite stays green, and CI is happy.

Nothing here is a bug. The gate did exactly what it was configured to do. The gap is between "cleared the bar" and "good" — a case where half the entity signal is missing still clears a bar set at 0.6, because two healthy scores carry one sick one.
steps.claudeSays: The runner emits one PASS/FAIL per case from overall >= 0.6. It never inspects which scorer sank, so a floor on the mean is not a floor on any individual dimension.

steps.title: The averaging that hides it
narrative: Zoom out and EC-001 vanishes. The scorer averages read 0.997 / 0.975 / 0.844 and the headline is 0.943. Nothing on that summary says a case scored 0.50 on entity resolution.

The category table is the only place the shape survives: edge_case averages 0.846 against entity_resolution's 0.982. That is the signal — edge cases are systematically weaker — and it is visible only because someone thought to break the average down.

The judge column is the honest one here. Its average, 0.844, is well below the two deterministic scorers, and it is the only scorer that moves much between cases. Averaging a model's opinion together with two string-matching checks flattens exactly the dimension you most wanted to watch.

after.title: AFTER — the same run, broken down

steps.title: The regression gate that confirms nothing moved
narrative: Then the comparison against the saved baseline: Previous avg 0.943 · Current avg 0.943 · Change +0.000 · No regressions detected · Unchanged: 20 cases. That is a real, useful result — it proves this change did not make the agent worse.

It proves nothing else. A regression gate measures movement, and EC-001 has been sitting at 0.744 in both runs. A weakness that was already there on the day you saved the baseline is invisible to it forever.

The lab's own footnote keeps this honest: "Exact scores may vary slightly depending on mock heuristics." These are mocked responses and a mocked judge, so treat the absolute numbers as a worked example and the structure — three scorers, a threshold, a category breakdown, a baseline diff — as the part you carry to a real agent.
steps.youDo: Raise overall >= 0.6 to 0.8 in eval_runner.py and re-run: EC-001 flips to FAIL and the suite goes red on the case you already knew was weak.
